2026-12-15.title: Tuesday after the Sunday of the Apparition to St Joseph
2026-12-15.alt: The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo continues.
2026-12-15.verse: For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.
theo: Paul came to Corinth, a city proud of rhetoric and philosophy, “in weakness and in fear and in much trembling.” He did not try to impress them: “I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.” His preaching was not plausible words of wisdom but “a demonstration of the Spirit and of power, so that your faith might rest not on human wisdom but on the power of God.” The crib and the cross are both foolishness to the world and power to those who believe.

Jesus warns his disciples of what lies ahead: they will be put out of the synagogues; some will even think that killing them is an offering to God. “I have said these things to you to keep you from stumbling.” Forewarned is forearmed. Christmas is not a sentimental holiday; the child of Bethlehem will be rejected, and those who follow him will share his rejection, and his victory.
outline: Point 3 · So that you may not stumble
live: Pray five minutes before a crucifix today.

2026-12-15.prayer: Lord Jesus, crucified and risen, be the centre of our faith. Free us from relying on human cleverness, let our faith rest on the power of God, and keep us from stumbling when trials come. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we proclaim Christ crucified. His weakness on the cross is the power of God that saves us.

2026-12-15.question: Is my faith built on cleverness or on Christ?

family.explain: Paul was a clever man, but he told people only about Jesus who died on the cross for us. God's power is greater than human cleverness.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who are persecuted.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we show God's love even to people who are unkind to us?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, crucified and risen, you are the power and wisdom of God. As we gather, strengthen us in weakness and give us courage in trials. Amen.
share: Paul decided to know nothing but Christ crucified (1 Corinthians 2:2). What is at the centre of my faith?
Jesus warned of persecution (John 16:2). How do I respond when I am treated unfairly for my faith?
Where do I rely on my cleverness instead of God's power?
pm.resp: Lord, your power is made perfect in weakness.
interc: For persecuted Christians in India and the world.
For those who persecute in God's name, that they may know the true God.
For preachers, that they may proclaim Christ crucified.
For those who feel weak and afraid.
For our group, that our faith may rest on the power of God.
pm.close: Lord God, your Son was crucified in weakness and raised in power. Strengthen persecuted Christians, convert their persecutors, and let our faith rest on you alone. Amen.

illus: In 1999 the missionary Graham Staines and his two young sons were burnt to death in Odisha. His widow, Gladys Staines, publicly forgave the killers and continued serving leprosy patients in India (H). Her forgiveness spoke of Christ crucified more powerfully than any argument.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul tells the Corinthians how he first came to them: I did not come proclaiming the mystery of God to you in lofty words or wisdom. For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified. I came to you in weakness and in fear and in much trembling (1 Corinthians 2:1–3).

Paul was a brilliant scholar, but he did not rely on cleverness. He preached Christ crucified with the power of the Spirit, so that your faith might rest not on human wisdom but on the power of God (1 Corinthians 2:5).

In the Gospel Jesus warns his disciples: they will put you out of the synagogues. Indeed, an hour is coming when those who kill you will think that by doing so they are offering worship to God. I have said these things to you so that when their hour comes you may remember that I told you about them (John 16:2–4).
Religious violence is not new. Jesus foresaw that some would persecute in God's name. Even today, Christians suffer in some places from people who believe they are serving God.

How should we respond? Not with clever arguments or with hatred, but like Paul: with Christ crucified, with humility, with the power of the Spirit. The Child of Yaldo will grow up to be crucified; his weakness is our strength.
During this fast, let us pray for those who persecute Christians and for those who suffer. And let us rely less on our own cleverness and more on the power of God. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus on the cross shows us the greatest love. Look at a crucifix today and say: thank you, Jesus!
